final_text:
Short answer: I cannot confirm that. In NHANES analyses available in ExposomeQL, there is no evidence that serum PFOA (LBXPFOA) is associated with higher TSH (LBXTSH) in 2015–2016, nor a 12% increase “above the median,” and NHANES is not suited to make a causal claim.

What the data show (from ExposomeQL tools):
- EP-WAS (survey-weighted meta-analysis across available NHANES cycles):
  - PFOA → TSH (LBXPFOA → LBXTSH), model 6 (age + age² + sex + ethnicity): no association returned (n_results = 0).
  - PFOA → TSH, fully adjusted model 2 (adds income + education): no association returned (n_results = 0).
- PFAS comparison against TSH (model 6): none of PFOA, PFOS, PFHxS, PFNA, or Me-PFOSA-AcOH showed a significant association with TSH (“no_association_found” for all).
- Reverse scan from TSH (fully adjusted): the only exposure associated at p < 1e-4 was a non-chemical marker (URXUCL, urine chlamydia). No PFAS appeared.

Important cautions for a regulatory citation:
- “Causes” is not appropriate for NHANES cross-sectional data; at most, one can state “associated with,” conditional on a prespecified model and multiple-testing context.
- The claim specifies a threshold effect (“above the median”) in a single cycle (2015–2016). The EP-WAS atlas tests continuous exposure models pooled across cycles; it does not support the stated >median, single-cycle, +12% result. Our attempt to run a custom, single-cycle, survey-weighted regression for 2015–2016 to recreate a >median contrast could not execute due to a temporary computation dependency issue, but the EP-WAS results already indicate no evidence of a positive association overall.

How you can phrase this in your document instead:
- “In NHANES, survey-weighted analyses in the EP-WAS atlas (age-, sex-, and race/ethnicity-adjusted; and fully adjusted models) do not show a statistically significant association between serum PFOA (LBXPFOA) and TSH (LBXTSH), including in analyses spanning the cycles where both were measured. No evidence supports a 12% higher TSH at exposures above the median in 2015–2016.”

Citable sources (from these tool calls):
- ExposomeQL EP-WAS search: LBXPFOA vs LBXTSH, model 6 and model 2 — no association found.
- ExposomeQL exposure comparison: PFAS (LBXPFOA, LBXPFOS, LBXPFHS, LBXPFNA, LBXMPAH) vs LBXTSH, model 6 — no association found.
- ExposomeQL reverse triangulation from LBXTSH — no PFAS among significant exposures.

If you need a single-cycle, threshold-based estimate for 2015–2016 (e.g., survey-weighted linear model of ln(TSH) on I[PFOA > median], with NHANES design weights and covariates), I can run and return the coefficient and 95% CI once the compute environment for custom NHANES code is restored. Please confirm:
- Adult age range to include (e.g., ≥18 years),
- Covariates (minimum: age, sex, race/ethnicity; optionally smoking/cotinine, BMI, income, education),
- Whether to model ln(TSH) and report percent difference for interpretability.
